The 80-token cap assumed about 1.6 tokens per word at the 49-word p95. Biomedical captions split into more subword tokens under a PubMedBERT-style vocabulary (17,825 distinct words). Also, 2.6% of captions exceed 60 words, which means 100+ tokens. Frozen features are computed only once, so a 128-token cap costs almost nothing extra and stops the longest captions being cut off. It stays well under the encoder's 256-token context. The same cap is used in all configs so they remain comparable.

rationale: BiomedCLIP was pretrained on PMC-15M, which consists of 15M figure–caption pairs from PubMed Central. This dataset is made of figure captions grouped by article, with UMLS-like concept codes. Its articles may therefore overlap the pretraining corpus, which would inflate the zero-shot score (0.966) and the gap to the other encoders (CCA ≤ 0.599 for non-BiomedCLIP pairs). The screening also used a pool of only 500 candidates. Test retrieval searches 5,000 candidates, so absolute R@10 will be lower. Finally, 18.7% of test samples share an article with validation samples, so selecting the model on validation may flatter test results slightly. This is not a train–test leak.

Retrieval is strong in absolute terms (mean R@10 0.871 vs chance 0.005, +0.111 over CCA with CI 0.098–0.124), but the trained primary is exactly the zero-shot BiomedCLIP solution: every configuration selected epoch 0 (the identity residual init), so training contributed nothing. Classification structure (ARI 0.509) equals zero-shot and is on par with the unimodal baseline (0.512). The results are adequate as a zero-shot solution, but the learned heads do not yet improve on it. In all trained configurations, validation R@10 drops right after the first epoch (primary 0.871 → 0.856 → 0.830) while training loss falls steadily (2.34 → 0.60). The same happens in contrastive_only, so the CE term is not the cause. At lr 1e-3, one epoch (about 40 steps at batch 512) moves the residual heads well away from an already well-aligned BiomedCLIP space; this data is likely close to BiomedCLIP's PMC pretraining distribution. A roughly 30× smaller learning rate with stronger weight decay keeps the heads near identity and gives the best chance of a small in-domain gain before overfitting starts. Partial fine-tuning is no option: it also degraded (0.853 after one epoch) and does not fit the 180 s per-fit cap. The revision costs 180 s of the 1140 s left, and the zero-shot result stands if validation does not improve.

alternatives_rejected.reason: Defensible, but the drop from epoch 1 onward clearly shows the learning rate is too high. A cheap single fit can test that, and it carries no downside risk because the original is kept if validation does not improve.
